title: Add maintenance mode toggles during restore (block writes + operator messaging + rollback)
author: Ethan Park
release_notes: Private DR/restore: `rw-private-dr` now supports maintenance mode toggles to block write paths during restore. Restore flow enables maintenance mode by default and prints actionable operator guidance + rollback steps.
pr_body:
Context
During in-place restores we need a consistent, reversible way to quiesce write paths so we don’t corrupt state while the control plane DB/artifacts are being restored. Operators were previously doing this manually (patching deployments / scaling components) which is error-prone and unclear.

This PR adds explicit “maintenance mode” toggles to the Private DR CLI and wires them into the restore flow with clear operator messaging and rollback steps.

What’s included
- New CLI surface:
  - `rw-private-dr maintenance enable` and `rw-private-dr maintenance disable`
  - `rw-private-dr maintenance status`
- Restore integration:
  - `restore execute` enables maintenance mode before DB restore begins (unless `--no-maintenance-mode`)
  - On successful restore completion, maintenance mode is disabled automatically
  - On restore failure, we keep maintenance mode enabled by default and print explicit rollback guidance (operator can pass `--disable-maintenance-on-failure` to revert automatically)
- Operator-facing messaging:
  - Prints what maintenance mode does: blocks writes, allows reads where safe
  - Prints expected API error behavior during maintenance mode (HTTP 503 with a Redwood-specific error code and actionable message)
  - Prints exact rollback commands to re-enable traffic safely
- Safety/guardrails:
  - If maintenance mode is already enabled, `restore execute` requires `--force` or explicit confirmation to proceed
  - `maintenance disable` requires `--confirm` unless `--yes` is set
  - Adds a best-effort “status reconciliation” step that verifies that the control plane reports maintenance mode enabled before continuing (with timeout + retries)
- Docs:
  - Updates `README.md` in repo with “restore preflight” section and maintenance mode explanation
  - Adds a short snippet intended for Confluence runbook linking (we’ll paste into the operator runbook after merge)

Implementation notes
- Mechanism: maintenance mode is toggled via the Private admin endpoint exposed by the control plane (same auth context as other `rw-private-dr` admin operations). This avoids direct k8s object edits in the common case and keeps the state source-of-truth in the control plane.
- The CLI prints:
  - the target cluster identifier
  - whether the CLI is using kubeconfig context or explicit endpoint
  - the current/desired maintenance mode state
  - next steps with copy/pastable commands
- We intentionally do NOT attempt to “auto-drain” external clients. Maintenance mode is a control plane behavior; traffic management (LB/DNS) stays an operator decision.

Out of scope
- Changing application-level routing/DNS cutover logic.
- Building a fully managed maintenance orchestration service.

How to test
1) Create a kind/minikube dev cluster and deploy the Private control plane.
2) Run `rw-private-dr maintenance enable --cluster <name>` and verify:
   - `maintenance status` reports enabled
   - write APIs reject with actionable error
3) Run `rw-private-dr restore execute ...` and verify maintenance mode is enabled before DB restore begins.
4) Induce a restore failure (e.g., bad object storage creds) and verify:
   - restore exits non-zero
   - maintenance mode remains enabled
   - CLI prints rollback instructions
5) Run `rw-private-dr maintenance disable --yes` and confirm writes work again.

Checklist
- [x] Unit tests for CLI args + status parsing
- [x] Integration test: toggling maintenance mode in a test cluster
- [x] Logs redact tokens/credentials
- [x] Docs updated

Links
- Linear: ENG-4904 (maintenance-mode API behavior and write-path blocking during restore)
- Related (control plane): redwood#18466 (API endpoint protection during maintenance/restore mode)

Notes for reviewers
- SRE: please focus on failure mode behavior and operator messaging.
- Security: please check that we’re not logging auth headers / tokens and that the confirmation prompts are reasonable for break-glass scenarios.
- Release Eng: confirm flags and defaults are compatible with upgrade/rollback backup gates.
commits: restore: enable maintenance mode before restore + default behavior on failure
control-plane client: add admin endpoint wrapper + retries/timeouts
docs: describe maintenance mode semantics + operator rollback steps
tests: unit + integration coverage for maintenance toggles
review_conversation: Rafael Mendes (review): Can we ensure we never auto-disable maintenance mode on failure? That’s a footgun if restore partially mutated state.
Ethan Park (author): Agree. Default is now: keep enabled on failure, and print explicit rollback. Added `--disable-maintenance-on-failure` as opt-in for advanced operators doing rehearsed drills.
Michael Nguyen (review): The retry loop waits up to 30s for status reconcile. Can we make this configurable? Some control planes can be slow under load.
Ethan Park (author): Added `--maintenance-timeout` (default 60s) and surfaced it in `restore execute` and `maintenance enable`.
Marcus Lin (review): Please confirm we’re not echoing bearer tokens in error logs when admin endpoint calls fail.

Ethan Park (author): Added header redaction in the HTTP client error path and a unit test asserting tokens never appear in logs. Also ensured we only log endpoint host, not full URL with query params.
Connor O'Brien (review): Flag naming: `--no-maintenance-mode` is fine, but docs should emphasize default behavior so operators aren’t surprised.
Ethan Park (author): Updated README “Restore defaults” section + added an explicit prompt line in CLI output: 'Maintenance mode ENABLED (writes blocked)'.
Sean Gallagher (review): Can we add a one-liner in the output pointing to the Confluence runbook section? Helps on-call.
Ethan Park (author): Added `Runbook: Private Restore (in-place) -> Maintenance Mode` placeholder link string; Docs will replace with canonical URL in the runbook page post-merge.
Rafael Mendes (approval): Looks good. Default behavior is safe and the rollback steps are clear. Approved.
Marcus Lin (approval): Security concerns addressed. Approved.
Michael Nguyen (approval): Approved after timeout flag. Thanks.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash merge by Ethan Park into main
